findings.title: Profile-weight pattern contradicts the slice's own "no per-agent loop" criterion
findings.description:
The prescribed weight construction, `np.array([profiles[pi].cohesion_weight for pi in state.profile_indices[eval_indices]])`, is a Python-level per-agent iteration inside every `BulkForce.__call__`. This conflicts in three places:
- **Technical requirement (line 198):** "No Python-level per-agent loops in any `BulkForce.__call__`".
- **Slice plan:** "O(1) Python overhead regardless of agent count".
- **Its own verification (lines 220-225):** the grep `for.*eval_indices` would match this line, so the design fails step 4 as written.

Fix: build a per-profile table and gather from it, e.g. `np.array([p.cohesion_weight for p in profiles])[state.profile_indices[eval_indices]]`. That iterates over profiles, not agents, and matches the architecture's "index-based dispatch / lookup tables" direction. Drop the "negligible at n=100 … precompute if needed" caveat.

findings.title: Padded-array memory claim is wrong for the clustering case the slice targets
findings.description:
The design says padding has no downside "at n <= 10K" and that memory matters at "100K+". But the slice's own premise is k → n under clustering, and `max_neighbors` is the per-tick maximum over all agents. At n = 10K fully clustered:
- each gathered `(n_active, max_neighbors, 2)` float64 array is about 1.6 GB, allocated per force per tick;
- `indices` adds about 800 MB and `mask` about 100 MB.

That is inside the architecture's "tens of thousands of agents on a single CPU process" target. It also runs against the architecture's notes on per-tick allocation and GC pressure. This does not require CSR now. The design should state the real bound (memory ∝ n_active × max_neighbors, set by the densest agent) and the agent-count/density envelope this slice supports. It should also say what happens beyond that envelope, and that must be an explicit failure, not silent degradation.

findings.title: Enumerated force list hides an ordering dependency with slice 103 and other `BulkForce` implementers
findings.description:
The plan requires "all existing implementations and callers update in the same slice", but the design hard-codes five neighbor forces plus three non-neighbor forces, and its loop-check grep covers only `flocking.py` and `herding.py`.
- **Slice 103:** it is `not_started` and precedes 109 in the plan. Its design specifies `FlightForce` and `PursuitForce` as per-agent loops over `neighbor_lists`, with per-force self-exclusion and per-neighbor dict lookups. If 103 lands first, 109's scope and verification miss those forces. If 109 lands first, 103's design is stale against the new protocol and the builder-level self-exclusion.
- **Slice 304:** its design shows an environment-aware force using the `neighbor_lists` signature, which is not in 109's list.

The design should state the intended order relative to 103 and define scope as "every `BulkForce` implementer present at implementation time", with the verification grep covering the engine force modules generally. The frontmatter lists 103 under `interfaces`, but the body never says what 103 must change.

findings.title: Equivalence criterion is under-specified against the tick-determinism goal
findings.description:
Per-force equivalence is `np.allclose(atol=1e-12)`, meaning outputs are not bit-identical to the loop versions. The integration test then requires positions and velocities "after N ticks match between old and new implementations", with no tolerance and no N. Flocking amplifies last-bit differences, so this test is either flaky or forces an arbitrary tolerance at implementation time. Two things to state:
- **Multi-tick test:** give the tolerance and N, or replace it with a single-tick comparison plus a repeat-run bit-identical check of the new implementation. The latter is what the architecture's tick-determinism goal actually requires.
- **Replay compatibility:** results change at the last-bit level versus pre-slice runs. The world server architecture relies on deterministic re-simulation for replay, so logs recorded before this slice will not reproduce exactly.

findings.title: MomentumForce is labelled "neighbor-dependent" but uses no neighbors
findings.description: Lines 35 and 190 group `MomentumForce` with the "five neighbor-dependent forces", while lines 125 and 201 say it reads no neighbor data. Its inclusion is correct, since the plan names it and it has a per-agent loop. Reword to "five loop-based forces" so the task breakdown does not apply the gather-mask-reduce pattern to it.

findings.title: Tick-budget success is verified only by a manual run
findings.description: The slice's primary value is ticks staying within 50ms after clustering, but this appears only in the walkthrough (a run of 5+ minutes), not under Technical Requirements. Adding it as a stated criterion would tie the slice's success to the NFR it exists to fix. A suitable form: tick duration within budget at the default config in a fully clustered state.
